prompt.text:
In `solution.rs`, implement a standard-library-only parser for an in-memory administrative command language.

Expose:

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Invocation {
    pub workspace: String,
    pub command: Command,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Command {
    Create { kind: Kind, name: String },
    Bundle { name: String, optimized: bool, tags: Vec<String> },
    Examine { name: String },
    Send { name: String, replace: bool },
    Check { jobs: u16 },
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Kind { Module, Dashboard }

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ParseError {
    MissingCommand,
    UnknownCommand(String),
    MissingValue(String),
    InvalidValue { option: String, value: String },
    DuplicateOption(String),
    Unexpected(String),
}

pub fn parse_invocation(args: &[&str]) -> Result<Invocation, ParseError>;
```

An optional global pair `--workspace VALUE` may occur only before the command; default workspace is `data`. Commands are: `create KIND NAME`, `bundle NAME [--optimized] [--tag VALUE]...`, `examine NAME`, `send NAME [--replace]`, and `check [--jobs VALUE]`. `KIND` is exactly `module` or `dashboard`. Jobs default to 1 and must parse as `u16` in 1..=256. Repeated `--tag` values are retained in encounter order and may be empty; all other options are single-use. Empty names and workspaces are invalid values. Missing option operands produce `MissingValue` naming the option. Unknown command words use `UnknownCommand`; extra positional values or misplaced/unknown options use `Unexpected`. An empty argument slice gives `MissingCommand`. Do not mutate input. Provide a new implementation; do not include `main`.

Return only the complete source file; do not include Markdown fences or prose.
